review_highlights.comment: Arguably the best course I've taken at Berkeley. If you are a CS/DS major, PLEASE TAKE IT. One of the few classes I genuinely loved. (Class also goes by CDSS 60)

Professor Roy is a fantastic instructor! Her energy, deep knowledge, and genuine care for students makes the class enjoyable and engaging. She encourages questions, supports creative topics for the panel presentation, and gives clear instructions. I learned a lot and always felt motivated to participate. Highly recommend her anthropology class!

Professor Roy is an invigorating lecture that has the rare ability to take abstract material and make it feel urgent. Easily the most though-provoking courses at Berkeley and should be required for CS/DS majors the way that it connects to debates on human values, AI and technology. She is kind, accessible and genuinely listens to her students.

HIGHLY recommend this class — covers a great deal about philosophical ideas and its intersection with modern data and ethics. Prof Roy is amazing, loves to chat with students in OH about anything in general! Classes and readings are highly intellectually stimulating and have genuinely inspired me to continue learning philosophy alongside my major!

It's a little late to be writing this since I took it in freshman year, but as I'm now graduating and looking back, this really was the last intellectually stimulating class on ethics in science & tech I took in college and I've had to take several to count towards my degree. Really pushed me and made me passionate about the subject area.

He recognized student effort, and is an excellent appraiser of acting skills.

Chris is a professor who has fundamentally changed my approach for acting. He is someone capable of molding himself depending on a student's personal needs, but still retains his strong beliefs in technique, rehearsal, and cultivating your instrument as an artist. I highly recommend him, whether you're seeking acting as a career, or even for fun.

Every acting student should strive to audition for Theater 111. This class helps students develop the way they think and talk about acting. Chris has given me confidence in my abilities by pushing me out of my comfort zone. As a graduating transfer student who has taken three classes with him, I can attest to his brilliance, wisdom, and kindness.

Professor Herold's classes are some of the best acting classes I have ever taken. He cultivates a space where you are pushed past what you think you can achieve, while caring for each and every actor in the class. Chris prepares you for auditions and working in the real, demanding industry, and genuinely wants to see you succeed.

Both of Chris's classes that I have taken have been deeply transformative. He makes acting feel like a tangible, step-by-step process, and the craft itself feel more accessible and more rewarding. He gives clear, honest, and respectful feedback. If you show up and put the work in, his class will be greatly impactful.

review_highlights.comment: Steve Fish is one of the most amazing Professors you will /ever/ have. I learned more from his Junior Seminar, Foundations of Political Thought and Action, than I have in any other class at Berkeley. He teaches not only material, but also develops our ability to think critically and apply theoretical concepts to real-world situations.

Prof. Fish is a very charismatic lecturer w/ incredibly engaging lectures and content. Class has a strict no-tech policy, and prompts for midterms and finals are released beforehand. Material got repetitive towards the end + he spends half an hour of class literally just answering questions, but still one of my favourite classes ever taken.

I took this class spring '25. It is very strict on attendance, participation, and tech. At first I was intimidated by the expectations and all of the readings; however, Prof. Fish is amazing at what he does. My GSI was also incredible.His lectures were great and this class helped build my passion for PoliSci. The difficulty is worth it.

favoritve intro course so far. u either love fish or hate him, he has a strong personality. for midterm prep u get 5 possible essay prompts, 3 will be on the test, you have to answer 2 which makes studying VERY STRAIGHTFORWARD (6/4/3 for final). STRICT no-tech policy w consequences. unfortunately not great at complying with DSP proctoring :(

I took his POLISCI5 in spring of ‘25 and I enjoyed the class a lot more than I thought I would. Definitely reading heavy and lots of participation in discussion is required, but I enjoyed the readings and my discussion GSI

analysis.name: Daniel Fisher
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Fisher takes such a revolutionary and important concept that is cultural anthropology and absolutely ruins it for his students. Lectures are incredibly dry, content is way too much for an intro anthropology class, and quizzes are way too difficult. All questions about grades are ignored on piazza and the class takes itself too seriously.

Even though 90% of the time his lectures are very unhelpful, the other 10% is when he tests specifically on what he discussed in the lecture. Halfway through our take-home, open note/lecture midterm, he suddenly removes all recorded lectures without warning. Some questions had material only discussed in the lecture. Highest p/np % with him ever.

Readings are very heavy, on average about 60-70 pages every week of difficult/ambiguous reading. Lectures very unhelpful and unclear + get removed in less than a week despite everything being online. Unless you get a good GSI you are basically screwed as quizzes/essays/tests test you on very specific things "mentioned" in lecture.

Spring 2022 Fisher taught the course online. Each week there were weekly readings that take hours to read. The initial part of the course was actually interesting, but then come the quizzes, midterms, and finals. Hours of reading, reviewing, to write these multiple questions essays. I wanted to focus on my technical classes, but couldn't b/c essay.

Fisher's lectures can be dense, but you'll adjust. If you do the readings and take good notes in lecture, you'll do well on the quizzes/midterm/final (open notes, graded by GSIs). The readings for homework each week weren't too long (avg. 50 pages per week) and often pretty interesting. Fisher and GSIs (Kyra was great!) are kind and helpful.

Lenient and supportive class. Four essays but your lowest gets dropped, and the last one is optional. Lots of detailed feedback and chances to heavily revise essays. Prof Flynn is an expert in modernism and although sometimes her explanations are a bit abstract, they are always insightful and she is extremely articulate. occasionally a bit difficult to contact via email outside of class,  but good office hours and she is a great teacher- funny, inspiring, really a dream professor if you like irish lit/modernism

Dr. Grosser is very knowledgeable and accessible outside of classes. He likes hardworking students and will help you a lot if you show genuine interest.
